notes: All four HVSs in Table 1 (HVS5, HVS7, HVS8, HVS1) are covered by the explicit group statement at T:p5-b1 that the HVSs are significantly unbound and that the four HVSs with known evolutionary state are discussed; HVS7, HVS8, and HVS1 are reanalyzed from prior measurements at T:p3-b3, and HVS5 is the paper's Keck/HIRES target. The subject heading at T:p1-b7 supplies the SDSS alias for HVS5. J0136+2425 is included as follow_up even though T:p4-b9 now finds it bound, because that passage says Tillich et al. (2009) discovered it as marginally unbound. HVS3 is named at T:p3-b3 but explicitly excluded from the discussion, and J1211+1437 at T:p4-b9 is only described as consistent with being bound without an explicit unbound-candidate statement; both are omitted.

HVS5: The abstract's statement of a "distance of 50 ± 5 kpc" (T:p1-b6) is not recorded as a separate heliocentric distance: the body gives a heliocentric distance of 44 ± 4 kpc and assigns 50 ± 5 kpc to the Galactocentric distance r_GC (T:p3-b7, T:p3-b10; Table I:p4-b0). The 50 ± 5 value is retained as galactocentric_radius. The paper reports only an approximate declination (+67°) and no precise RA, parallax, proper-motion components, or bound/unbound probabilities. The Galactic rest-frame speed is explicitly a minimum from radial velocity alone and may be larger if tangential motion is present (T:p2-b13, T:p5-b3).

HVS8: For HVS8, Table 1 reports the Galactocentric distance r_GC = 60 ± 10 kpc. The paper does not report HVS8 heliocentric distance, parallax, equatorial position, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability in the supplied material; values for those quantities are not inferred or calculated. Evidence is from Table 1 (T:p4-b0 / I:p4-b0).

HVS1: HVS1 is not the paper's primary target, but it is included in Table 1. No heliocentric distance, parallax, right ascension, declination, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported specifically for HVS1.

HD 271791: The target star HD 271791 appears only in Section 3.3 (T:p4-b8) as part of the comparison sample of unbound runaways: "HD 271791 is an unbound 11 M_⊙ B star. The observed proper motion shows it was ejected in the direction of rotation from the outer disk (Heber et al. 2008a). The star has an age of 25±5 Myr and a flight time from the disk of 25±6 Myr. Formally, the star has t_arr = 0±8 Myr." No numerical right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper-motion components, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star (it is not listed in Table 1, which contains only HVS5, HVS7, HVS8 and HVS1). The paper describes it qualitatively as "unbound" and gives its mass (11 M_⊙), age (25±5 Myr), disk flight time (25±6 Myr) and arrival time (0±8 Myr), but none of these correspond to the requested quantities and no quantitative probability of being unbound is given. Therefore no eligible quantity values are extracted for HD 271791.

HIP 60350: The paper mentions HIP 60350 only in T:p4-b8, describing it as a marginally unbound 5 M⊙ B star with an age of 45^{+15}_{-30} Myr and a disk flight time of 14 ± 3 Myr (hence t_arr = 31^{+15}_{-30} Myr). It reports no right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for HIP 60350, so no eligible quantities are retained.

J0136+2425: The supplied identifier J0136+2425 corresponds to the "marginally unbound 2.5 M_sun A star J0136+2425" attributed to Tillich et al. (2009) and discussed briefly in Section 3.3 (T:p4-b9). For this star the paper reports only a derived age (245 Myr), a flight time of 12 Myr "if it comes from the disk", its 2.5 M_sun mass, and a qualitative statement that, accepting modern Milky Way halo masses of ~1.7x10^12 M_sun, "it is bound to the Milky Way and may be explained as a halo star". None of the requested quantities (position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, bound/unbound probability) is numerically reported for this star; the binding statement is qualitative and no probability value is given, so no quantities are retained. (The paper's own high-resolution analysis concerns HVS5 = SDSS J091759.47+672238.35, a different object.)
